gotchas: This is the group with the least evidence and the most risk. Do not assume the two-lead red/black pattern from the diaphragm pumps applies here just because it is the same vendor — that is precisely the family-name reasoning the catalogue rules forbid.

A '24V submersible solar deep well pump' is the shape of product that sometimes ships with a separate MPPT-ish or dry-run controller box, and sometimes does not. Missing evidence, stated plainly, so the next person knows what to go find: (1) the SEAFLO model number on the label of each, (2) a SEAFLO manual for either, (3) whether either ships with a controller in the box, (4) lead count and colours.

No pressure switch means no self-regulation. Unlike the 51/52/53/42 group, a relay left closed on one of these runs it until something fails. Any rule that powers one of these must own the dry-run and the run-time limit itself.

The SEAFLO manual library does list 'Control Systems' and 'Security System' categories — SFWAS1-20-03, SFWAS2-10-03, SFWAS1-20-01, all water-level alarm systems. None of them is a model in this sweep, and an alarm system with contacts is not a communication interface. Noted so nobody chases it as a protocol lead.
